Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
data.description:
Key points:
  • ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
  • Judges say genocide can coexist with military aims
  • South Africa says ruling sets important precedent for state genocide

By Anthony Deutsch and Stephanie van den Berg

The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over the war in Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective.

While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before the World Court are based on allegations that states breached their obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention.

On Thursday, the court found that Myanmar had violated the convention on multiple grounds stemming from mistreatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority by the armed forces.

South Africa, which has brought a genocide case against Israel over its conduct in Gaza, welcomed the judgment. Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola said it set an important precedent by establishing for the first time that a state had committed genocide. He said it was of "great significance" to the case against Israel, which is not expected to be argued until 2029.

Both Myanmar and Israel have defended the actions of their armed forces as legitimate responses to insurgencies. But a majority of nine judges on the 15-member bench found that around 10,000 killings, including of children, the razing of homes, widespread sexual violence and the forced exodus of more than 700,000 people in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.

The ruling also handed other major legal victories to Gambia, which brought the case seven years ago on behalf of Muslim-majority countries.

The judges found that Myanmar had failed in its obligation to prevent genocide and said it must facilitate the return of Rohingya refugees and pay unspecified reparations.

The court also adopted conclusions from UN fact-finding reports, including one stating that mass deaths and rapes showed genocidal intent.

IMPORTANT PRECEDENT

Israeli legal scholar Yuval Shany said the ruling could broaden the arguments available to South Africa in its case against Israel.

He said the court maintained a requirement that genocidal intent be the “only reasonable inference,” but expanded the contextual factors it can consider beyond a pattern of conduct, to include the scale and systematic nature of acts and the history of persecution.

The approach “gives South Africa more avenues to argue for genocide” in Gaza, Shany said.

Proving genocide is notoriously difficult because it requires establishing an "intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such."

Five criminal acts can constitute genocide: killing members of a group, causing them serious bodily or mental harm, creating conditions calculated to destroy them, preventing births, or forcibly transferring children to ​other groups.

Lamola said South Africa would study the judgment carefully with a view to demonstrating, as the court had in the Rohingya case, that a state's actions, including ethnic cleansing, the killing of children, sexual violence and destruction of civilian infrastructure, can fall within the definition of genocide.

TARGETING OF CHILDREN, WOMEN

Another aspect of the ruling that could resonate in the Israel case was the court's emphasis on the systematic nature and scale of the crimes committed in Myanmar, said Marieke de Hoon, professor of international criminal law at the University of Amsterdam.

South Africa alleges that Israel's military operations created conditions intended to prevent births and disproportionately affected women and children in Gaza. In its filing to the ICJ, it said an estimated 70% of those killed were non-combatants. Israel rejects those allegations and says its operations have been conducted in accordance with international law.

"Arguments that a military intent or military objective would erase the idea that there could be a genocide intent are now rejected by the court," said De Hoon.

She said the judges found that some acts, including attacks on children and women and sexual violence, could not be explained by military objectives alone, leaving genocide as the only reasonable inference.

The Hague Initiative for International Cooperation (Thinc), a think tank funded by pro-Israeli groups, said the judgment would fundamentally alter how courts assess allegations of genocide by imposing a "lower threshold for proving genocidal intent, with serious consequences for Western militaries engaged in confronting terror," such as after Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

It is "not only a verdict in a particular case but a template," Thinc's director, Andrew Tucker, wrote in a reaction.

"Its propositions will be used in future cases: that genocidal intent may coexist with legitimate military objectives...that UN reports compiled without access can carry decisive weight; and that a state can breach the duty to prevent genocide without any finding that genocide occurred."

While the World Court judgment unequivocally found Myanmar responsible for genocide, proving the crime in court remains difficult, said Richard Horsey, senior adviser for Asia at the International Crisis Group.

"The ICJ has never before found that a state committed genocide. The legal bar is extremely high, but what this case shows is that it is surmountable,” he said.

data.title: Nvidia Falls Behind Alphabet, Loses $2.3 Trillion In Market Value Since October Peak
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares were on track to post a seven-day losing streak if losses hold till market close on Friday.
  • The company’s market capitalization has dropped about 41% from its early October peak.
  • Nvidia held the top spot among U.S. companies for much of the year before its recent decline in market value.

Nvidia’s (NVDA) market capitalization fell behind Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) in morning trade on Friday, making it the fourth most valuable U.S. company.

NVDA stock was down 4.6% in morning trading, extending a seven-day losing streak and hitting a fresh 16-month low, while GOOGL stock rose around 2.5%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia trended in ‘extremely bullish’ zone over the past day, while sentiment around Alphabet trended in the ‘bearish’ zone.

Alphabet’s market value was $3.44 trillion at the time of writing, against $3.41 trillion for Nvidia, a gap of about $30 billion.

Nvidia’s market value peaked near $5.7 trillion in early October, and is now about 41% below that level.

Technology Stocks Lead Market Declines

U.S. equities were mixed in morning trade on Friday. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) was down 0.76%, the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) gained 0.36%, while the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) plummeted over 2%. Retail sentiment around QQQ on Stocktwits trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day.

The weakness extended across the semiconductor sector. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell 5.7%, with Credo Technology Group (CRDO) and Coherent (COHR) leading losses. CRDO stock and COHR were both down around about 10%.

Micron Technology (MU) declined 9.5%, while Broadcom (AVGO) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) fell more than 7%.

Nvidia’s Strong Results Have Not Stemmed the Slide

Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and above analyst estimates of $108.7 billion, according to Koyfin. Earnings per share came in at $2.68, compared with estimates of $2.47.

The company projected revenue of $130 billion for the January quarter and raised its growth outlook to 75% from 70%. Despite the strong results and outlook, the stock has continued to decline.

The leadership transition continued to add to the uncertainty surrounding the company. Nvidia disclosed last week that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO, with Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress appointed interim CEO.

Apple Remains The Most Valuable US Company

Apple (AAPL) remained the most valuable U.S. company, with a market capitalization of about $5.08 trillion, according to Koyfin. Microsoft (MSFT) ranked second at $3.73 trillion, followed by Alphabet and Nvidia.

Amazon (AMZN) ranked fifth, with a market value of approximately $2.80 trillion, around $615 billion below Nvidia.

Nvidia held the top spot among U.S. companies for much of the year before its recent decline in market value.

data.title: GREENROW OPENS NEW STORE IN PALO ALTO
data.description:
GreenRow, a portfolio brand of Williams-Sonoma, Inc. (), the world’s largest digital-first, design-led and sustainable home retailer, announced today the opening of the brand’s second retail store located at Town & Country Village in Palo Alto, California. The new Palo Alto location follows GreenRow’s debut flagship store in New York City’s SoHo neighborhood, which opened earlier this year and was recently named one of House Beautiful’s “Best Home Stores in America.”

Launched in 2023, GreenRow offers thoughtfully designed home furnishings made with an emphasis on craftsmanship, responsible sourcing, and lower-impact production. The brand prioritizes innovative manufacturing practices and low-impact materials wherever possible, while supporting at least one of Williams-Sonoma, Inc.’s social or environmental initiatives. Responsibly sourced linen, cotton, wood, and recycled materials are featured throughout the assortment, along with handmade and artisanal pieces that showcase the unique qualities of their materials and craftsmanship.

The GreenRow Palo Alto store’s assortment of furniture, lighting, textiles, rugs, tabletop, and décor showcases the brand’s belief that sustainability should not require a compromise in style, comfort or individuality. Products featured in the store are designed to bring warmth, character and style to every room in the home in a responsible and considered way. Customers who visit the new store can also shop a curated collection of vintage, found and one-of-a-kind pieces, while receiving complimentary design services and personalized guidance from GreenRow’s design experts.

“Our stores are a destination for inspiration and a place where customers can explore beautiful products, learn more about the materials behind them to help curate a home that feels both personal and purposeful,” said Jaimee Seabury, Vice President of GreenRow. “We look forward to welcoming the South Bay Area community into a space that showcases GreenRow’s commitment to craftsmanship, creativity and making sustainable design more accessible, inspiring and relevant to everyday life.”

To celebrate the new store opening, GreenRow will host a grand opening weekend from Friday, November 20, through Sunday, November 22, 2026. The celebration will be open to the public, and a portion of net proceeds from opening weekend sales will be donated to Filoli Historic House & Garden.

For more information about GreenRow or the new Palo Alto store, please visit: www.GreenRow.com.

GreenRow is a mission-driven home furnishings brand that creates modern heirlooms that balance beauty, comfort, and integrity—proving that design can be aspirational and responsibly made. Every product in the GreenRow assortment supports at least one of Williams-Sonoma, Inc.’s social or environmental initiatives and is made using innovative, low-impact manufacturing practices wherever possible. The collections showcase a commitment to craftsmanship and prioritize responsibly sourced materials—including linen, cotton, wood, and recycled fibers—selected for their quality, durability, and reduced environmental impact.

Williams-Sonoma, Inc. (), a Fortune 500 and S&P 500 company, is the world’s largest digital-first, design-led and sustainable home retailer. These brands collectively support The Key Rewards, the company's loyalty and credit card program that offers members exclusive benefits. The company operates in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom, and has unaffiliated franchisees that operate stores in Mexico, South Korea, India, and the Philippines.

data.title: BJ's Wholesale Raises Outlook, but Promotions Weigh on Margins — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Connor Hart

BJ's Wholesale Club raised its full-year outlook after reporting higher profit and revenue in the recent quarter. However, the results weren't quite as strong as the headline numbers suggest.

The warehouse club operator benefited from a litigation settlement, proceeds from which it used in part to fund an aggressive promotional campaign that weighed on margins. Adjusting for the benefit and other items, quarterly earnings underwhelmed investors.

Shares fell 3.8%, to $106.50, Friday. Despite the decline, the stock is up nearly 16% year to date.

Chief Executive Bob Eddy said on a call with analysts that consumers remain resilient, as traffic improved and spending increased across all income levels. A key sales driver was BJ's 42nd-birthday promotion, which offered members 42% off select items throughout its stores.

Total revenue jumped 17.5% to $6.28 billion in the latest quarter, topping Wall Street models for $5.97 billion. Comparable-club sales, which account for store openings and closings, increased 4.1% excluding gasoline sales. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for a 2.9% gain.

The promotion also weighed on merchandise margins, though, which declined 170 basis points from a year earlier. BJ's estimated the promotion cost about $56 million, an expense it said was fully funded by proceeds from the litigation settlement.

The quarter included a roughly $240 million pretax benefit from a litigation settlement tied to credit-card interchange fees. BJ's previously disclosed the settlement in September and said the benefit would be reflected in its third-quarter results.

"We did not view the settlement as just an amount of cash," Eddy said. "We viewed it as an opportunity to invest in BJ's stakeholders, and we chose to play offense with it."

The company additionally invested about $95 million during the quarter in employee compensation, advertising and labor, partially offsetting the settlement benefit. Those investments, coupled with the birthday promotions, were intended to strengthen customer engagement and support long-term growth, Chief Financial Officer Laura Felice said.

BJ's reported a profit of $219.5 million, or $1.73 a share, for the third quarter ended Oct. 31, compared with $152.1 million, or $1.15 a share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings also were $1.73 a share, well ahead of analyst expectations for $1.26 a share.

But JPMorgan analysts said the headline earnings figure required some "math olympics" to unpack. After adjusting for merchandise-margin investments, selling, general and administrative expense benefits, and a sale-leaseback gain, the bank estimated earnings were closer to $1.20 a share.

For the full year, BJ's now expects adjusted earnings of $5.10 to $5.30 a share, compared with its previous forecast of $4.60 to $4.80 a share. The company also raised the low end of its forecast for comparable-club sales growth excluding gasoline to 2.5% from 2%, while maintaining the high end at 3%.

Analysts are looking for adjusted earnings of $4.74 a share as well as comparable-club sales growth of 2.6%.

data.title: U.S. Consumer Sentiment Improves More Than Previously Estimated November
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - A report released by the University of Michigan on Friday showed consumer sentiment in the U.S. improved by more than previously estimated in the month of November.

The University of Michigan said its consumer sentiment index for November was upwardly revised to 51.5 from a preliminary reading of 51.0.

With the upward revision, which came in line with economist estimates, the index came in further above the final October reading of 48.0.

'Current personal finances improved for low-wealth consumers and, to a lesser extent, middle-wealth consumers, who experienced some relief with falling gas prices,' said Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu.

She added, 'In contrast, those with the largest stockholdings reported a decline in personal finances, consistent with continued AI-related agitation in stock markets.'

Hsu noted the consumer sentiment index remains 9 percent below the reading seen prior to the start of the Iran conflict in February, 'reflecting continued uncertainty regarding the cost-of-living factors that dominate consumers' perspectives.'

The report said the current economic conditions index climbed to 49.4 in November from 46.7 in October, while the index of consumer expectations jumped to 52.9 in November from 48.8 in October.

With regard to inflation expectations, the University of Michigan said year-ahead inflation expectations plunged to 3.7 percent in November from 4.7 percent in October.

Hsu noted year-ahead inflation expectations remain meaningfully above the 3.4 percent seen before the Iran conflict began in February along with all 2024 readings.

Long-run inflation expectations also dipped to 3.3 percent in November from 3.5 percent in October but are still higher than the 2024 range of 2.8 to 3.2 percent.

'Despite the softening in inflation expectations, consumers continue to report overwhelmingly that inflation-rather than unemployment-will cause greater hardship for consumers in the next one or two years,' Hsu said.

About Ferro-Alloy Resources Limited:

The Company's operations are all located at the Balasausqandiq deposit in Kyzylordinskoye Oblast in the South of Kazakhstan.

Balasausqandiq is a very large deposit, with vanadium as the principal product together with the CBS and several by-products. Owing to the nature of the ore, the capital and operating costs are very much lower than for other vanadium projects.

The most recent mineral resource estimate for ore-body one (of seven) provided an Indicated Mineral Resource of 32.9 million tonnes at a mean grade of 0.62% vanadium pentoxide ("V2O5") equating to 203,364 contained tonnes of V2O5. In the system of reserve estimation used in Kazakhstan the reserves are estimated to be over 70 million tonnes in ore-bodies 1 to 5, but this does not include the full depth of ore-bodies 2 to 5, or the remaining ore-bodies which remain substantially unexplored.

The grade of carbon in the deposit is over 8%. The carbon flows through to the tailings from where it is concentrated, in a simple low-cost operation, into a 40% carbon product, the CBS, that can be used in place of carbon black as a reinforcing filler in the making of rubber.

The Project will be developed in two phases, Phase 1 and Phase 2, with Phase 1 treating 1.65 million tonnes per year.

The results of the feasibility study, carried out principally by SRK and Tetra Tech, were announced in October 2025, showing a project net present value ("NPV") of US$748m and internal rate of return ("IRR") of 22%.  Since then, a preliminary re-estimation of the capital costs by Chinese engineers China National Chemical Engineering Sixth Construction Co., Ltd has been received, which would have the effect of increasing NPV to US$932m and IRR to 31%.

There is an existing concentrate processing operation at the site of the Balasausqandiq deposit. The production facilities were originally created from a 15,000 tonnes per year pilot plant, which was then expanded and adapted to recover vanadium, molybdenum and nickel from purchased concentrates.  Alongside this operation, there is a well-equipped laboratory and highly skilled technical team, who have already developed the technology that is being built into the feasibility study and is further developing and optimising processes needed for future vanadium and carbon operations. The plant will operate only when profitable concentrates are available and, when not operating as a production facility, will operate on an expanded basis as an R&D centre.

data.title: PayPal Turns to Amex Exec to Take Reins at Venmo — Market Talk
data.description: PayPal is bringing in a new leader for Venmo, its popular payments app that generates meager profits, as part of a broader executive reshuffling. Kartik Mani, who currently serves as president of global network and partner services at American Express, is joining PayPal as president and head of consumer financial services and Venmo. Turning Venmo into a one-stop money-management app, with tools for consumers to keep budgets and invest, is central to plans by PayPal's CEO, Enrique Lores, to run the company as a stand-alone business after a proposed buyout from Stripe and Advent International valued at more than $50 billion stalled. (colin.kellaher@wsj.com)

data.title: Bank of Canada Expected to Raise Rates Once More Even as Consumer Spending Softens — Market Talk
data.description: Consumer spending in Canada is likely to slow in the near term amid softness in the labor market and the squeeze on household incomes from elevated fuel prices and modestly tighter financial conditions, Oxford Economics' Michael Davenport says. The economist notes a weak flash estimate for October retail sales adds to a litany of softer-than-expected data releases since the Bank of Canada raised interest rates in late October. Still, he expects a federal grocery and essentials supplement will give a one-time boost to spending in early 2027. And Davenport continues to expect the central bank will lift its overnight rate a further quarter percentage point in December before moving to the sidelines for an extended pause. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

data.title: A hard landing could be triggered by aggressive rate hikes – BofA
data.description:
Bank of America analysts are warning that the Federal Reserve's aggressive rate tightening cycle risks triggering a hard landing for the economy, with GDP and earnings-per-share growth forecasts likely facing downward revisions.

In a soft-landing scenario, the S&P 500 (SP500) below 7,000 is an attractive buying opportunity, with market breadth improving by spring. If so, investors can position for a shift from rate hikes to cuts by moving into cyclical assets like crypto, chips, copper, consumer stocks, and real estate.

However, BofA analysts believe the likelihood of a hard landing remains underappreciated—they expect GDP and earnings-per-share forecasts to be revised downward and warned that the current AI-driven capital expenditure and wealth-driven “boom loop” could flip into a “doom loop” that forces investors to reduce stock allocations.

For now, with uncertainty elevated, investors are retreating to what they already own and clustering in low-volatility, defensive value positions as they wait to see which scenario unfolds.

BofA drew striking parallels to the 2000 tech bubble, noting that markets were trading in “bubble” territory back in May but are now trading "post-bubble."

During the 2000 bubble's aftermath, staples , utilities , and financials were the biggest outperformers with returns between 45% and 60%, while tech and telecoms were the largest underperformers with returns around -50% and -40%.

The analysts warn that "Fed hikes led to recession and proper bear markets in 2001," and with voters demanding “affordability” through midterm elections, the March 18th or April 28th FOMC meetings represent the earliest points when investors can discount the tightening cycle ending.

The research identified two key economic drivers now under pressure: U.S. household equity wealth, which is down approximately $5T quarter-to-date though still up roughly $8T in 2026, and AI capital expenditure from hyperscalers forecasting $1.3T in spending despite negative free cash flow.

BofA noted that "voters, bond markets, asset allocators are all saying 'slow AI data center buildout,'" which threatens the growth narrative supporting current market valuations.

For recession signals, BofA analysts pointed to unemployment claims and credit spreads as "always best recession tells."

Specifically, claims exceeding 250,000 and investment-grade spreads surpassing 100 basis points would signal the “boom loop” has become a "doom loop," forcing asset allocators to cut stocks and increase allocations to bonds, China, the U.S. dollar, and assets negatively correlated with AI such as real estate—a strategy the analysts describe as "long condos, short chips."

data.title: Klarna partners with Adyen on agentic AI checkout
data.description:
Klarna and Adyen said on Friday shoppers can now pay with Klarna when an AI agent checks out for them through Adyen's agentic suite. It's the first payment option beyond cards available in Adyen Agentic.

Up until now, most AI shopping agents complete purchases with a stored credit or debit card, which precludes flexible payment options that many shoppers choose at regular checkout.

Adyen Agentic and merchants that already offer Klarna through Adyen can switch it on with no new integration work, the companies said.

With Klarna as a payment method within Adyen Agentic, the agent shows shoppers the same Klarna options the merchant already offers, such as paying in full, in interest-free installments, or with financing. Shoppers review and confirm every purchase before it is completed.

Klarna stock slipped 2.3% in morning trading as PayPo, a Polish rival, prepares for a potential initial public offering in Warsaw. Adyeb rose 0.6% in U.S. trading.
